summary_blocks.body:
In 16Personalities’ NERIS framework, INFP-A is the Assertive Mediator. The -A marks the end of the Identity scale associated with greater self-assurance and less sensitivity to stress. The official MBTI code has four letters, INFP.

In the Myers–Briggs framework, INFP stands for Introversion, Intuition, Feeling and Perceiving. In NERIS, Assertive (-A) and Turbulent (-T) are opposite ends of the Identity scale.

Two people can check the same draft and make the same correction. Afterwards, they might feel differently about how well they did. Identity describes that kind of self-evaluation and response to pressure. It does not establish skill or accuracy.

| --- | --- |
| Where the suffix belongs | -A stands for Assertive in 16Personalities’ NERIS Identity scale. |
| Relation to the four letters | Official MBTI uses INFP without an A/T suffix. |
| What it describes | Self-assurance and responses to pressure in NERIS. |
| What it cannot establish | Writing skill, empathy, judgment accuracy or the strength of Fi or Ne. |
| What to reflect on | What did the feedback identify? How confident did you feel after checking it? Record the two separately. |
| Interpreting one reaction | One submission or criticism cannot establish a result on Identity. |

| Question | What INFP-A describes |
| --- | --- |
| Where the suffix belongs | -A stands for Assertive in 16Personalities’ NERIS Identity scale. |
| Relation to the four letters | Official MBTI uses INFP without an A/T suffix. |
| What it describes | Self-assurance and responses to pressure in NERIS. |
| What it cannot establish | Writing skill, empathy, judgment accuracy or the strength of Fi or Ne. |
| What to reflect on | What did the feedback identify? How confident did you feel after checking it? Record the two separately. |

sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
Read the [INFP profile](/en/personality/infp) for the four-letter code and its function notation. The A here is the NERIS suffix.

The Myers–Briggs letters refer to inward attention (I), patterns and possibilities (N), values and effects on people in decisions (F), and openness to new information in the outside world (P). Writing is one setting in which to illustrate those ideas.

Identity concerns how someone tends to evaluate themselves and respond to pressure. A change in confidence after a submission can illustrate that experience. Rereading or revising cannot establish the suffix.

After correcting the same issue in a draft, one writer might feel sure about the rest of it, while another might feel less sure. The correction is the same in both cases.

### How Assertive and Turbulent differ within NERIS

NERIS describes the Assertive end as more self-assured and less sensitive to stress. It describes the Turbulent end as more self-doubting and sensitive to stress.

People at either end can ask for details, reread a draft and revise it. The number and order of those actions do not identify the suffix.

The same writer can feel at ease with a private draft and take more care with a submission. Audience and stakes can change what the writer does.
sections.title: INFP-A letters and framework

sections.body_md:
In a fictional reading group, someone calls a short piece about the author’s grandmother too personal for a review. The writer can ask: “Are you concerned about the personal detail, or about whether the piece makes its argument?”

After checking the same passage, a writer closer to Assertive might feel sure about the rest of the piece. A writer closer to Turbulent might feel less sure about it. Either can ask the same question and make the same revision.

| Situation | What to try | What to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sharing an unfinished draft | State what kind of feedback you need | Confirm the reader knows what is still open |
| Receiving vague criticism | Ask for the passage and what the reader took from it | Get another relevant reader’s view if the issue remains unclear |
| Hearing a challenge to your position | Explain the evidence and experience behind your view | Check factual objections against the original material |
| Getting several objections | Sort comments by evidence, argument and style | Check whether repeated concerns point to the same issue |
| Seeing a reader interpret your words differently | Explain what you meant and ask what they read | Check whether the intended audience would read it that way |

A confident writer can revise several times. A quiet writer can have a firm view. Audience, stakes and the review process can explain either response.
sections.title: INFP-A core patterns, value and counterexamples

sections.body_md:
A/T cannot tell you whether a role fits. Compare the work itself, the feedback you would receive and the responsibilities you would hold.

Try a small writing or editing task. Ask how often someone will review it, how they define a good result and how much say you have in the content. A clear brief can give anyone a better basis for deciding what to revise.

Ask whether the objection concerns the evidence or the conclusion. Check the original material and explain why you drew the conclusion. Then decide what needs to change.

### INFP-A at work or study: writing confidence in a discussable form

Invite feedback on a specific part of the work, whether you feel sure of it or still have doubts.

When you share a draft, say what it is trying to do, what it relies on and where you would like feedback. In a fictional class, a student asks the tutor to focus on the weakest section first.

If a reader calls a paragraph confusing, ask where they lose the thread. Try one revision and see whether another reader understands it.
sections.title: INFP-A work and career exploration

sections.body_md:
Talk directly about commitments, contact and boundaries. Speaking clearly and hearing the other person’s response both matter.

In a fictional conversation, a partner asks for more time to think. Ask whether anything needs clarifying now, then agree when to revisit the decision.

In a fictional collaboration, one writer wants to preserve the wording and the other loses track in the third paragraph. Ask which idea needs to stay and where the wording gets in the way.

### INFP-A: how to explain a view and invite feedback

You can explain why you hold a view and identify what you are open to changing.

Try stating the conclusion, the evidence and what you would change. For example: “I’d like to keep what my grandmother said here. We can revise the wording around the quotation.”
sections.title: INFP-A relationships and communication

sections.body_md:
People closer to the Assertive end can still feel intense pressure or second-guess themselves. How often someone submits or revises does not tell you how they feel.

Notice what is getting harder: revising a passage, replying to a message or opening the comments. Consider workload, deadlines and the stakes involved.

In a fictional group, someone dismisses a draft without saying why. Write down the actual comment and ask whether there is a specific concern you can address.

If the same task keeps spilling into time you had set aside for other things, consider discussing the deadline or asking for help. If distress persists or disrupts sleep, mood or daily life, consider speaking with a qualified professional.
sections.title: INFP-A stress and recovery

sections.body_md:
Write what you meant, what the reader understood and what changed after any revision.

Choose a piece of feedback and record how confident you felt before and after clarifying it. Keep the reader’s interpretation separate from your confidence. Neither record alone establishes the quality of the piece or your A/T result.

Stop when you understand the concern and have decided whether a revision would help. If the records start to feel like a score you have to improve, set them aside.

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources.** [16Personalities’ framework description](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) says NERIS uses a five-scale model without Jungian cognitive functions. Its [Identity overview](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent) describes Assertive and Turbulent. MBTI Form M counts cover the four-letter codes and cannot establish proportions for NERIS A/T.

**Function-stack convention.** The Myers & Briggs Foundation’s type dynamics describes INFP’s dominant Fi, auxiliary Ne and inferior Te. It allows Si or Se for tertiary Sensing. The notation on this page uses Si. These positions cannot establish task order or ability.

**Editorial fiction.** The reading group, class draft, conversations and reflection exercise are fictional. They illustrate possible responses without establishing how often they occur.

**Scope.** Read a result in the context of the instrument and answering conditions. The suffix cannot be used to rank ability, screen job applicants or predict relationships. FermatMind uses its own questions and scoring. See the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

FermatMind Editorial

sections.title: INFP-A related types and comparisons

items.answer:
A stands for Assertive in 16Personalities’ NERIS Identity scale. It describes self-assurance and responses to pressure. Official MBTI uses the four letters INFP.

Someone can clarify a criticism and revise a passage while still feeling confident about the rest of the work. Someone else can take the same steps and feel less sure. One instance cannot establish the suffix.
items.question: What does the A in INFP-A mean?

items.answer:
F names the Myers–Briggs Feeling preference, which considers values and effects on people in decisions. A names the Assertive end of NERIS Identity.

Fairness to the reader can be one writing criterion. How confident you feel about the draft after submitting it is a separate question.
items.question: The third letter of INFP-A is F. Is that related to the A?

items.answer:
Someone can take feedback seriously and still feel sure about their judgment. A/T does not tell you how much weight they give someone else’s advice.

In the same fictional group, two writers could both note every comment. One may remain confident about their draft, while the other may feel less certain.
items.question: Is INFP-A necessarily less concerned with what others think than INFP-T?

items.answer:
In the type-dynamics convention used here, INFP has dominant Fi and auxiliary Ne. NERIS does not use a function stack, and its A/T scale does not measure Fi or Ne.

If you want to improve a piece of writing, look at the work and ask for specific feedback. The suffix cannot assess your writing.
items.question: Are Fi and Ne stronger in INFP-A?

items.answer:
Find out whether the person disputes the evidence or the conclusion. Someone at either end can ask for details, reconsider or explain why they disagree.

Try asking, “Do you think an example is missing, or do you disagree with the argument?” Use the answer to decide what needs attention.
items.question: INFP-A: when your position is challenged in person, should you give ground first?

items.answer:
An early draft can be useful if sharing it fits the assignment and the reader knows what feedback you need. Formal submission may require further checks.

Say which section is ready and which still needs review. The requirements of the task determine whether the draft is ready to share.
items.question: INFP-A: is handing something in after one pass too hasty?

items.answer:
Yes. Someone closer to the Assertive end can still feel pressure or doubt a particular decision.

In a fictional group, a wording suggestion might feel easy to address, while public criticism of a personal piece might feel much harder. Neither response determines A/T.
items.question: Can INFP-A also doubt itself repeatedly and feel a lot of pressure?

items.answer:
Read the [INFP profile](/en/personality/infp) for the four preferences, [INFP-T](/en/personality/infp-t) for Turbulent, or the [same-type comparison](/en/personality/infp-a-vs-infp-t) for a side-by-side example.

If two reports differ, check the instrument, version and answering conditions before comparing the labels.
items.question: What should I read next about INFP-A?

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources.** [16Personalities’ framework description](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) says NERIS uses a five-scale model without Jungian cognitive functions. Its [Identity overview](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent) describes Assertive and Turbulent. MBTI Form M counts cover the four-letter codes and cannot establish proportions for NERIS A/T.

**Function-stack convention.** The Myers & Briggs Foundation’s type dynamics describes INFP’s dominant Fi, auxiliary Ne and inferior Te. It allows Si or Se for tertiary Sensing. The notation on this page uses Si. These positions cannot establish task order or ability.

**Editorial fiction.** The reading group, class draft, conversations and reflection exercise are fictional. They illustrate possible responses without establishing how often they occur.

**Scope.** Read a result in the context of the instrument and answering conditions. The suffix cannot be used to rank ability, screen job applicants or predict relationships. FermatMind uses its own questions and scoring. See the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).
